target.title: feat(android): render LaTeX display math in chat via bundled KaTeX
target.body:
Related: #100699

## What Problem This Solves

Delivers the declared Android math follow-up: `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` blocks in assistant responses rendered as typeset math instead of raw TeX, matching the iOS display-math behavior from #100829.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dependency decision first: jlatexmath-android (the only native Android LaTeX library lineage) is GPL-2.0 and archived since 2023 — unusable for store distribution. Instead, KaTeX v0.17.0 (MIT) ships as bundled assets (minified js/css + required woff2 fonts only; no Gradle dependency): the release archive's SHA-256 matches GitHub's published digest, per-file hashes are recorded in an assets README, and the licenses screen gains a KaTeX entry (MIT + SIL OFL font note) per the Android licenses policy.

Rendering keeps WebViews out of the transcript entirely: one process-singleton offscreen WebView (attached as a transparent 1px view per Android's visible-state contract, lifecycle-detached) renders queued math jobs into bitmaps that transcript rows display as plain `Image`s, cached in a byte-bounded LRU keyed by latex/width/dark-mode, with negative caching and a 3s per-job timeout falling back to code-style raw text. The WebView is locked down: an asset-allowlist request interceptor returns empty responses for anything not under `file:///android_asset/katex/`, LaTeX reaches KaTeX only as a JSON-encoded `evaluateJavascript` argument (never HTML concatenation) with `trust:false`, `throwOnError:true`, `maxExpand:1000`, and the only JS bridge is a render-completion callback. The process singleton retains only an Application-backed WebView and a weak activity host that detaches on destruction. Segmentation mirrors the iOS contract exactly: top-level blocks only, never inside code, unclosed math stays plain while streaming, 5000-byte cap falls back.

## User Impact

Android users see typeset display math in finished assistant messages; streaming, code blocks, and oversized/invalid math keep today's plain-text behavior. Android's licenses screen credits KaTeX.

## Evidence

- 38 focused tests green across segmenter (25: delimiters, code protection, streaming, caps), renderer protocol (8: queue ordering/dedupe, cache keying incl. dark mode, negative results, timeout fallback — WebView bridge injectable), packaged renderer fallback contract (1), and license notices (4).
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwy132f27yajdr0494ge03j7`: Play + ThirdParty unit suites, both debug APK assemblies, both lint lanes, benchmark assembly, app and benchmark ktlint all passed after rebase.
- Asset integrity: archive digest `f77cf2…4b88` matches GitHub's published release digest (independently re-verified via the releases API); per-file sha256s in `assets/katex/README.md`.
- Local API 36 emulator, exact rebased Play APK: valid assistant display math rendered as typeset KaTeX; malformed `\frac{` stayed raw in the code-style fallback; chat remained responsive after background/foreground. Screenshots were inspected locally and not uploaded because image-upload approval was not provided.
- Security boundary reviewed and accepted for this narrowed implementation: bundled assets only, network blocked, strict asset URL allowlist, no HTML interpolation, `trust:false`, bounded expansion/bitmap/cache, Application-only process lifetime, weak/detached activity host.
- Fresh structured Codex autoreview — clean after the malformed-input and Android lint fixes.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound outbound upload file reads to configured media limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`uploadImageFeishu` and `uploadFileFeishu` accept a string file path, but they previously called `readRegularFile({ filePath })` without a `maxBytes` limit. A huge or symlinked local file could be read into memory unbounded before the Feishu SDK upload attempt, causing gateway OOM or denial of service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's documented default upload limit is 30 MB. The gateway already computes `mediaMaxBytes` from `account.config.mediaMaxMb` (default 30 MB) in `sendMediaFeishu`, but it was not forwarded to the string-path readers. This change caps string-path reads to the same bound so malformed or oversized local attachments fail early with a clear size-limit error instead of exhausting process memory.

## User Impact

- Outbound Feishu image/file uploads from a local path are now bounded by the configured `mediaMaxMb` limit (default 30 MB).
- Oversized path inputs are rejected before any network call, with the existing "file exceeds limit" message from `readRegularFile`.
- Buffer inputs continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added `maxBytes?: number` to `uploadImageFeishu` and `uploadFileFeishu` and forwarded `mediaMaxBytes` from `sendMediaFeishu`.
- Added regression tests in `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` covering:
  - string path reads pass the configured `maxBytes`;
  - oversized string paths are rejected and no SDK upload is attempted.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
  # 48 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I ran the Feishu media test suite, including the new `uploadImageFeishu / uploadFileFeishu string-path bounds` tests. String paths are now read with the configured `maxBytes` cap before the Feishu SDK upload call:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |extension-feishu| extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts (48 tests) 1819ms
     ✓ uploadImageFeishu passes maxBytes when reading a string path
     ✓ uploadImageFeishu rejects oversized string paths
     ✓ uploadFileFeishu passes maxBytes when reading a string path
     ✓ uploadFileFeishu rejects oversized string paths
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  48 passed (48)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.00s
```

- Normal string-path reads forward `maxBytes` to `readRegularFile` and then call the Feishu SDK.
- Oversized string paths throw before `client.im.image.create` / `client.im.file.create` is invoked, so no network upload is attempted for a rejected local file.
